answers.answer: DotLn is a local-first compiler and runtime that works with any model. It takes a person's judgment (their taste, standards and corrections) and turns each piece into a small mechanism for AI teams that can be inspected. Each task gets only the rules it needs. Hard rules are enforced outside the model, and a record of what happened is kept so it can be replayed. The page says it is not an agent, an agent harness or an orchestration layer. It calls itself an "agentic platform": a shared base where people and software actors hold work, authority and evidence.

answers.answer:
The source prepares version v0.73.1. What runs today:
- A deterministic kernel and compiler turn a loadout graph into a bounded program, with an authority envelope checked on every decision. A typed reactor folds durable events into state that can be replayed.
- The Repo Gardener + Seiri scenario runs end to end from a JSONL event log. It refuses deletion structurally and has a separate fake verifier check its candidates.
- Disposable worker episodes on Claude Code and Codex have changed a synthetic module in isolated worktrees, passed its host test and committed, with a blinded verifier judging the change.
- The `publish` and `vertical` commands can open a pull request under an operator grant, and run the loop from a filed issue through review triage. So far this has only happened in recorded scratch proofs.
- A resident host dispatches bounded episodes and holds further dispatch when a mission check finds drift. It is not an installed service, and it has no measured payoff curve.
- A browser evidence adapter collects screenshot, DOM, network and console witnesses.
- An `intent` command files draft work orders.
- An actor board, a text console and a live console are available.
- The repository itself runs on this same machinery.
quotes: A deterministic kernel and compiler turn a loadout graph into a bounded program and an authority envelope that is checked on every decision, and a typed reactor folds durable events into replayable state.
The Repo Gardener plus Seiri scenario runs end to end from a JSONL event log, refuses deletion structurally and verifies its candidates with a separate fake verifier.

answers.answer: Run `npm install` first, then the one command `npm run skeleton` runs the first proof. In it, a Repo Gardener with the Seiri mechanic inspects a fixture repository while the operator is away. It is refused the deletion it tries, a separate fake verifier checks its candidates, and it stands down when the operator returns. The output is a numbered timeline, a line of glyphs and a receipt.

The page suggests a starting point by interest:
- For the idea, the vision doc (docs/product/00-vision.md).
- For the machinery, the domain model (docs/product/02-domain-model.md) and the architecture (docs/product/03-architecture.md).
- To see something moving, the skeleton README (packages/skeleton/README.md).

It also points to the operator playbook (docs/PLAYBOOK.md) for the whole loop, the roadmap, and CONTRIBUTING.md for the toolchain and tests.
